TL;DR - Mods are awesome, imo. Do you agree?

I recently bought State of Decay for 5 dollars on Steam during the sale. I HIGHLY recommend it, so much so that I bought the DLC for it! I've sunk almost 30 hours into the bloody thing, and I can't stop playing!

One thing that nagged me, though, was the fact that the Zombies run, a lot. Yes, they do the signature stumble, but they also run, which is sad. I understand special zombies being able to do so, but come on, really? I was hoping for a slow menace! Time to prepare, but also impending doom! Well, on a whim, I did a google search for SoD mods, and found that it's actually supported (and actively used) on the Nexus. And, lo and behold, I found my slow zombie mod! I'm currently ecstatic!

So my question is, when you think mods, what games do you think, and do you think they ruin the experience, or enhance it? Obviously Bethesda titles come to mind, but I want to hear all about your favorite mods!
"Mods ruin games"... This statement is completely untrue.
Dude mods are the best, it basically comes down to the question "Does extra content ruin a game?" We all know the obvious answer.
I would wholeheartedly agree with you there! Some of the best games out there even STARTED as mods, so that's saying something!
The Dark Souls PVP didn't fare well when mods came into play. Other than that, I can't think of anything that is 'ruined' by mods.

The best games are mods.

DoTa was a mod which in turn created league of legends and DoTa 2. The most competitive MoBa's and then you have counter-strike which was also a mod and also the most competitive FPS.

Next after that...Day Z was a mod and look how popular that is which is now basically spawning it's own genre of games (Rust, H1Z1, 7 Days to die).

Oh and while I'm thinking about it, Insurgency started as a mod and is the best FPS I've ever played.

so yeah mods are awesome if I thought about it more I could come up with countless examples like CoD 4 > MW2 and BF2 > BF3/4

That is such a general term that I don't think either statement can be true.

mods can do much or so little in countless ways that saying it one way or the other can be right in any given situation.
Honestly this depends on the game and mod in question. Mods can be bugfixes, which are only ever desired. Mods can also let people cheat through the game.
I bought Battlefield 1942 just to play Desert Combat. Sometimes the mod is the game.

Do mods ruin the experience? Sure, sometimes but you know what? That's the users choice. Someone wants to make a Skyrim item that gives them god-like abilities? It's not for me but that doesn't matter.

Mods in general however are a plus.

One of the best examples I can think of is ACE2 for Arma 2. It takes a teamwork based milsim side of Arma and throws it in the deep end of realism.

Mortars or artillery for example go from an "artillery computer" system that has a lot of similarities to Battlefield 3 mortars to a system that requires actual calculation to determine the azimuth and deflection to the target either using an ingame ballistics calculator or by hard math. The gun or tubes themselves require a team to operate; one to operate the weapon and determine it's orientation, another to orient the gun or gun and at least one to prep, set the charge and load rounds.

From my experience, it's a hugely satisfying feeling to see players pull it off... almost every accurate strike is met with hoots and hollers from the people around me in game. Without mods frankly you would never see something like that because it caters to a very specific niche of people who demand realism, one that otherwise isn't a commercially viable target for game developers.
For single player games, mods are great. I wouldn't use them in multiplayer games that aren't Garry's Mod but that's about it.
